summary: Notice and talk about patterns in situations full of data.
Show data with sorted objects, drawings or tally marks and share what they notice.
Compare two objects by a shared attribute to see which has more, less or the same.
Describe measurable traits of objects, such as length and weight.
Sort objects by shape, size, color and thickness.

Read, write, compare and order numbers 0 to 31; see teen numbers as ten and ones.
Count forward to at least 31 and backward from 20.
Find the number that is one more or one less than a given number.
Solve and show addition and subtraction stories within 10 with objects, drawings or equations.
Split numbers up to 10 into pairs in different ways and record with drawings or equations.
Add and subtract within 5 fluently.
Tell if one group has more, fewer or the same number of objects as another.

Spot, make, finish and extend simple repeating or growing patterns of shapes, sounds or numbers.
See patterns in counting and skip count by tens from 0 to 100.
Notice data patterns and pose statistical questions with teacher help.
Collect data for a question and show it with drawings, tallies and simple bar graphs.
Describe events as impossible, possible or certain.
Order three objects by length and compare two lengths using a third object.
Measure length using non-standard units.

Count forward and backward from any number up to 120.
Describe numbers 10 to 120 as some tens plus ones.
Estimate amounts up to 120 using benchmarks of fives and tens.
Solve addition and subtraction stories within 20 with unknowns in any position.
Add within 100, two-digit plus one-digit or a multiple of ten, sometimes making a new ten.
Split numbers up to 10 into pairs in more than one way and record them.
Add and subtract within 20 using strategies like making ten; fluent within 10.
Use pairs that make ten to add up to the next decade, through 100.
Find the double of any one-digit number.
Share a set of items equally between two groups and call each share a half.
Compare two two-digit numbers using tens and ones.
Decide if addition and subtraction equations are true or false, even with operations on both sides.
Find the unknown number in an addition or subtraction equation with three numbers.
Make simple patterns and find rules to continue them; calculators may help explore.
Skip count by 2s and 5s from zero to 120 and by 10s from any number.
Describe what changes and what stays the same in a growing picture pattern.
Notice data patterns and write statistical questions.
Decide what counts as data for a question and see that data can vary.
Collect data and show it with drawings, picture graphs, dot plots or technology.
Make predictions from patterns in data displays.
Tell the difference between possible and likely.
Estimate lengths in inches, feet, centimeters and meters.
Measure how much longer one object is than another in standard units.
Pick and use tools like rulers, yardsticks and tapes to measure length.
Show whole numbers, sums and differences within 100 on a number line.
Split a rectangle into rows and columns of equal squares and count them.
Add and subtract within 100 to solve length problems using drawings and equations.
Name coins including quarters, total their value and write amounts with $ and ¢.
Classify flat and solid shapes by counting faces, sides, edges and vertices.
Draw or build basic flat shapes such as triangles, trapezoids and hexagons.
Describe where one object is in relation to another.
Count collections up to 1000 by grouping tens and hundreds and record the count.
Read, write, compare, order and represent whole numbers up to 1000.
Mentally find 10 or 100 more or less than a three-digit number and explain.
Describe numbers up to 1000 as hundreds, tens and ones; 100 is ten tens.
Estimate sums and differences of two-digit numbers.
Add and subtract within 1000 with models and place value, linking to written methods.
Add and subtract two-digit numbers flexibly with place-value strategies and explain why they work.
Add and subtract within 20 fluently using mental strategies.
Use landmark tens to add up to 100 and subtract from 100 fluently.
Share items equally among 2 or 4 groups and name halves and fourths.
Compare two- and three-digit numbers using hundreds, tens and ones.
Write number sentences with unknowns for situations and solve them using addition-subtraction links.
Make and justify claims about addition and subtraction using true/false and open equations.
Find and describe number patterns from repeated adding, skip counting and arrays.
Skip count by 2s and 5s from any number up to 120.
Write number expressions that describe a growing picture pattern.
Notice data patterns and ask statistical questions that data can answer.
Explain ways to collect data such as surveys, grouping and measuring.
Collect and organize data, handle missing values, and display it, including with technology.
Make predictions and see that the amount and source of data affect accuracy.
Analyze tables, bar graphs, picture graphs and line plots with scales to support claims.
Describe events as impossible, unlikely, equally likely, likely or certain.
Measure lengths to the nearest quarter unit.
Compare the sizes of units within one measurement system, like inches, feet and yards.
Find the perimeter of a polygon with whole-number sides.
Add and subtract to make change up to one dollar in different ways.
Draw regular and irregular polygons with a given number of sides.
Mentally find 100, 1000 or 10,000 more or less than a number and explain.
Describe numbers up to 100,000 by place value.
Compare and order whole numbers up to 100,000 using <, = and >.
Estimate sums and differences up to 1000 using benchmarks and place value.
Add and subtract within 1000 with flexible place-value strategies and explain them.
Model and solve multiplication and division stories with one-digit factors using pictures.

Split circles, rectangles and the 0-to-1 number line into halves, thirds, fourths and eighths.

Make change up to $20 using $ and ¢ correctly.

Use relational thinking to find missing values in multiplication and division sentences.

Find volume and surface area of solids built from unit cubes.

# MDE 2022 Minnesota Academic Standards in Mathematics (Final) - official PDF: https://education.mn.gov/mdeprod/idcplg?IdcService=GET_FILE&dDocName=PROD086145&RevisionSelectionMethod=latestReleased&Rendition=primary (Wayback 20260306043314); K-5 benchmark tables pages 13-67.

# MDE 2022 standards spreadsheet (adopted February 28, 2025): https://education.mn.gov/mdeprod/idcplg?IdcService=GET_FILE&dDocName=PROD086360&RevisionSelectionMethod=latestReleased&Rendition=primary (Wayback 20260306045706); used to recover formulas that the PDF renders as images (4.1.2.2, 4.3.5.11, 4.3.5.12, 5.3.5.5, 5.3.5.7, 5.3.5.14-16). Texts otherwise identical; the spreadsheet lists 3.3.5.01 twice.

# MDE Shifts in the 2022 Academic Standards in Mathematics: https://education.mn.gov/mdeprod/idcplg?IdcService=GET_FILE&dDocName=PROD098789&RevisionSelectionMethod=latestReleased&Rendition=primary (Wayback 20260306061224).

# MDE Math Standards Implementation page: https://education.mn.gov/MDE/dse/stds/Math/imp/ (Wayback 20260306045108); MDE Mathematics page https://education.mn.gov/MDE/dse/stds/Math/ (Wayback 20260825094942).

# Minn. R. 3501.0750: https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/3501.0750/ ; MDE timeline: https://education.mn.gov/mdeprod/idcplg?IdcService=GET_FILE&dDocName=PROD081270%20&RevisionSelectionMethod=latestReleased&Rendition=primary.

# Which set is in effect: MDE Mathematics page (education.mn.gov/MDE/dse/stds/Math/, read via Wayback snapshot 2026-08-25 because the live site returns a bot-check page) says, in summary: the 2007 K-12 math standards went into effect July 2007 and are in effect through the 2026-27 school year; the 2022 standards go into effect by the beginning of 2027-28.
# Same page: MCA-III math (grades 3-8, 11) assesses the 2007 standards; MCA-IV assessing the 2022 standards is first given in 2027-28.

# Minn. R. 3501.0750 (published 2025-09-03, 49 SR 1123), subp. 6, says districts must implement these (2022) standards by the beginning of the 2027-2028 school year. The rule text holds only the anchor standards; benchmarks live in MDE's standards document.

# The 2007 rule parts (Minn. R. 3501.0700-3501.0745) now show as [Repealed, 49 SR 1123] in the rule book, yet MDE still states the 2007 standards are in effect through 2026-27; we follow MDE's statement.

# MDE Recommended Implementation Timeline (PROD081270) calls 2025-26 and 2026-27 transition years and suggests starting 2022 benchmarks early in grades K-1 (2025-26) and grade 2 (2026-27); it says districts set their own transition, the requirement being full implementation in 2027-28.
# This file: the 2022 Minnesota K-12 Academic Standards in Mathematics, NOT required until 2027-28 (2007 set in mn.tsv is in effect for 2026-27).

# Code format: grade.strand.anchor-standard.benchmark. Kindergarten is grade 0 (0.2.4.3). Anchor standards are numbered 1-7 across all strands, so the third digit is never reset per strand. Codes here follow the official PDF and grade-level PDFs (no zero padding: 1.2.3.3, 1.3.5.10); MDE's spreadsheet zero-pads the benchmark number (1.2.3.03). Each benchmark ends with practice tags (MP1-MP8) and context symbols, omitted here.

# Strands (2nd digit): 1 Data and Probability; 2 Spatial Reasoning; 3 Patterns and Relationships. Anchor standards (3rd digit): 1 Data Sciences, 2 Chance and Uncertainty (strand 1); 3 Measurement, 4 Geometry (strand 2); 5 Number Relationships, 6 Equivalence and Relational Thinking, 7 Patterns and Relationships (strand 3).
# Skipped: Dimension 1 Standards of Mathematical Practice (MP1-MP8) and Dimension 2 benchmark contexts, which carry no grade content of their own.
# Row counts: 188 benchmarks; same 65, edited 61, moved 22, new 40.

# CCSS K-5 standards not referenced by any row: K.OA.A.4 K.G.A.3 K.G.B.5 1.OA.A.2 1.OA.B.3 1.OA.B.4 1.OA.C.5 1.NBT.C.5 1.NBT.C.6 1.MD.B.3 2.OA.C.3 2.NBT.B.6 2.MD.A.2 2.MD.C.7 3.MD.A.1 3.MD.A.2 3.MD.C.5 4.OA.B.4 4.NBT.B.4 4.NF.C.5 4.MD.C.7 4.G.A.3 5.NBT.A.4 5.NF.B.6 5.MD.A.1. Notably: no telling time at any K-5 grade (1.MD.B.3, 2.MD.C.7, 3.MD.A.1; MDE's Shifts doc confirms time was dropped), no rounding (3.NBT.A.1 only via estimation, 5.NBT.A.4 absent), no lines of symmetry (4.G.A.3), no unit conversion (5.MD.A.1), no standard algorithm for add/subtract (4.NBT.B.4), no liquid volume/mass (3.MD.A.2), no dividing unit fractions by whole numbers in grade 5 (5.NF.B.7 only partly via 5.3.5.16).

# Notable non-CCSS content: data science and probability every grade K-5 (statistical questions, predictions, likelihood scales, frequency tables, mean/median/range in grade 5); financial literacy (3.3.5.13 saving goals, 4.3.5.17 money decisions, 5.3.5.18 payment methods, 5.3.5.19 budgets and debt); visual growing patterns and figure-n rules (1.3.7.3, 2.3.7.3, 4.3.7.1, 5.3.7.5); relational-thinking open sentences; 3-D views and nets (4.2.4.4-5, 5.2.4.2); triangle/parallelogram area and surface area in grade 5; numbers to 100,000 in grade 3; multiplying within 144 in grade 3; ratio tables in grade 5.

# Uncertainties: x.1.1.1 data-pattern and statistical-question benchmarks marked new (CCSS starts statistical questions in 6.SP.A.1) though K-5 CCSS has related graphing standards; relational-thinking benchmarks mapped to grade-1/3 equation standards as moved (2.3.6.3, 3.3.6.1, 4.3.6.1) while 5.3.6.1 is new; 5.3.5.16 (n divided by a/b) mapped to 5.NF.B.7 as edited though CCSS grade 5 limits to unit fractions; 2.3.5.5 estimation mapped to 3.OA.D.8 as moved. Summaries are paraphrases, not official text.
# Mapping notes: no official Minnesota-to-CCSS crosswalk exists (Minnesota did not adopt CCSS math); all ccss values are this file's own judgment from reading both texts.

# kind: same = CCSS standard at the same grade with essentially the same content; edited = same-grade CCSS counterpart but range, scope or emphasis differs (extra codes from other grades may be listed); moved = only CCSS counterpart is at another K-5 grade; new = no CCSS K-5 counterpart (includes content CCSS places in grade 6-8; those codes are not listed because only K-5 codes are allowed).
# ccss codes are listed at standard level (no sub-letters such as 4.NF.B.4a).
